narrative.title: The Archive Index Lookup
narrative.scenario: A robotic archivist stores shelf labels in one strictly increasing index and must fetch the exact shelf holding a requested call number. Because the index is sorted, the robot can discard half of the remaining shelves after a single probe instead of walking the aisle. Report the shelf position when the call number exists, or signal that it does not.
narrative.inputFormat: An array nums of n integers sorted in ascending order with distinct values, and an integer target.
narrative.outputFormat: The 0-indexed position of target in nums, or -1 when target is absent.
constraints: All values in nums are unique
nums is sorted in ascending order

testCases.explanation: Probing the middle shelves repeatedly narrows the search to index 4, where 9 lives.
The search space collapses to an empty range without ever matching 2, so the lookup reports -1.

hintLevels: Level 1: Every probe should make the remaining candidate range roughly half as large.
Level 2: Keep two bounds and move one of them past the middle probe each round based on whether the target sits above or below it.
Level 3: Compute the middle as low plus half the distance between the bounds so it cannot overflow, and make sure the loop still runs when the bounds meet on a single element.
